identity.lineage: The owner asked whether Closing Time could be improved to fix the Saturday open or fit the trains better on a weekday, and to give the answer a new name. Closing Time has four on at the Saturday open, the rules' minimum, where Short Run has five, and its weekday fit is 36.4 against Short Run's 29.1, because its three 13:30-22:30s put an extra person on the quiet 20:00-22:00 floor. Those are where Closing Time found its minutes: with a 16:00 closer, today's times pay the contract with only 180 minutes a week to spare, and a 13:45 every weekday leaves the week 145 short. The owner had already set the closer's start aside ("whether it is 1545 or 1600 doesn't matter"), and a 15:45 closer pays the minutes the 13:30-22:30s were there for. Searching the weekday and Saturday tables (final-table.mjs, exhaustive on a pool of 35 shift times at every weekday total from 7,440 to 7,480 minutes, with five at each opening) and laying each on Closing Time's own rest days (exact-rota.py) found the best of them that can still be worked without breaking anything Closing Time keeps: the 14h 35m rest, no fatigue factor, every factor's value Closing Time's or better except the one count a fifth Saturday opener must raise (FF2, 29 to 30, Short Run's), the weekends, the runs, the leave. The weekday fit comes to 29.8, the Saturday 9.6 with five at the open, and 18 weeks sit on one shift time; the costs are a Saturday fit of 9.6 against 8.7, the price of the fifth person at the open, a sixth new shift time, a week-to-week step of 1h 13m (Closing Time 1h 10m), a lightest week of 25h 30m (27h 00m), which Closing Time's rest days force on any table without a nine-hour late, and a closer a quarter of an hour longer.
